policy: extension mapping is a pinned in-code table (never the platform mimetypes registry) with case-insensitive lookup: .csv -> text/csv (never application/vnd.ms-excel), .yml AND .yaml -> application/x-yaml, .svg -> 'image/svg+xml; charset=utf-8' (the charset suffix is required - XSS pentest finding), .js -> text/javascript; unknown extensions -> application/octet-stream (never text/plain); no-extension names, bare-trailing-dot names and plain dotfiles (.env) -> octet-stream, but a dot-leading name with a real extension (.config.yaml) maps by that extension
bug_report: The analytics team's CSV exports open garbled in Excel for some users but not others, an embedded image on the docs site intermittently renders as raw text, and a build-pipeline config artifact was displayed inline by the browser instead of downloading. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix content_type so served assets get the intended types, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: pin content_type's MIME table - text/csv, x-yaml both spellings, svg charset, octet-stream fallback
decision_rationale: All three asset tickets traced to content_type guessing types registry-style. The policy pins an in-code table - deterministic on every machine, never the platform mimetypes registry - with a case-insensitive extension lookup (lowercase before the lookup; .JPG, .CSV and .Html are all real inputs). Pinned overrides: .csv is text/csv - never application/vnd.ms-excel, the Windows-registry fossil that garbled the analytics exports; .yml AND .yaml both map to application/x-yaml; .svg is exactly 'image/svg+xml; charset=utf-8' - the charset suffix is required, mandated by the XSS pentest finding, because svg is markup; .js is text/javascript per the WHATWG registry, not application/javascript. Anything not in the table returns application/octet-stream - never text/plain, the fallback that displayed a leaked build artifact inline. A name with no extension, a bare trailing dot, or a plain dotfile like .env has no extension and returns octet-stream, but a dot-leading name with a real extension (.config.yaml) maps by its real extension.
